A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same Token Assorted study. Methods, experiments, equations, figures, and appendices can be matched reliably. Earlier Appendix E becomes Appendix F; later Appendix E is new.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and evaluation results for maze planning, logical reasoning, and mathematical reasoning in Tables 4.1-4.4, with additional DART-MATH results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds compression-rate experiments in Table 4.5 and decoded model-generation examples in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The VQ-VAE architecture and objective, partial left-to-right replacement, randomized replacement lengths, and language-model training procedure are unchanged. The compression-rate sweep tests an existing parameter; the added VQ-VAE deployment paragraph clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same maze, logical-reasoning, and mathematical datasets, including MetaMathQA and DART-MATH training. The compression sweep uses existing benchmarks, and the new arithmetic examples remain within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the synthetic, main mathematical, replacement-strategy, and DART-MATH comparisons. The added compression study reuses CoT as its baseline. Newly cited planning-token work is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds evaluation configurations with compression rates r=2 and r=32 alongside the existing r=16 setting on Llama-3.2-3B. Existing experiments retain their splits, training budgets, decoding procedures, and accuracy/token-count metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds a compression-rate sensitivity study on one model (Table 4.5 and Figure 4.2) and two cases examining decoded latent tokens (Appendix E). These are focused extensions to the retained replacement-strategy ablations, attention analysis, and generation examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The added experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 4.1-4.4 and the relocated DART-MATH results are unchanged. Table 4.5 adds r=2 and r=32 results, with reported average accuracy/token counts of 27.08/595.6 and 27.9/481.4, respectively. Appendix E adds two successful responses with decoded latent fragments.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, replacement equation, VQ-VAE objective, and Appendix B notation are unchanged. The new sensitivity discussion and decoded arithmetic examples introduce no formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: partial discrete-latent reasoning compression, randomized adaptation to latent tokens, and improved accuracy with shorter traces. The headline results and claimed average 17% trace reduction remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly interprets r=16 as balancing abstraction against information loss. Appendix E argues that decoded fragments capture reasoning intentions and can trigger subsequent reasoning despite grammatical errors. Existing attention-based explanations and the impact statement are retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly states that the VQ-VAE has 50 million parameters and is used during data preparation, while the LLM generates latent tokens without it during inference. This adds implementation clarity; Appendix A settings and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. (2023), Guiding Language Model Reasoning with Planning Tokens, with a short related-work description, and cites Su et al. (2025), GaLore 2, in the introduction. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include a short implementation clarification, new Section 4.4, an expanded and numbered Section 4.5, and the new interpretability appendix. Cross-references and conference front matter are updated, but most existing prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4.5, the dual-axis compression trade-off plot in Figure 4.2, and two boxed decoded examples. Existing visuals are retained, with local layout reflow and Appendix E tables relabeled F.1-F.2.

improvement.justification: The compression study provides evidence for a previously untested design choice, decoded examples make latent content inspectable, and the VQ-VAE clarification improves implementation understanding. These are useful but limited gains: the sweep covers one model without uncertainty estimates, and interpretability rests on two noisy examples. Table 4.5 also leaves accuracy averaging unexplained: the new r=32 scores have an unweighted mean of about 28.37, versus the reported 27.9.
